## Week 8: additive models, trees and ensembles

How some flexible fits are built, and how to read them. An additive model fitted one curve at a time, each to what the others leave; partial dependence and ICE plots, which show one input's part in any fitted model and can hide an interaction. A tree built one greedy split at a time, then pruned. Bagging and random forests: the variance of an average of correlated trees, and the out-of-bag error. Permutation importance, why permuting an input can mislead, and leave-one-covariate-out importance. Boosting as gradient descent, one small tree at a time. Data: IMDb films ([data note](data/movies.html)).

**Reading**

- ISLR Chapter 8 (Tree-Based Methods), section 8.1, pp. 327–340, all of it this time: regression trees again, pruning, classification trees, trees against linear models.
- ISLR Chapter 8, sections 8.2.1–8.2.3, pp. 340–348: bagging (with out-of-bag error and variable importance measures), random forests, boosting. Section 8.2.4, Bayesian additive regression trees, is not part of the course.
- ISLR Chapter 7, section 7.7.1, pp. 307–310, re-read: fitting an additive model one predictor at a time (backfitting).
- IML, [Partial Dependence Plot (PDP)](https://christophm.github.io/interpretable-ml-book/pdp.html): the sections "Definition and estimation", "Examples" and "Limitations".
- IML, [Permutation Feature Importance](https://christophm.github.io/interpretable-ml-book/feature-importance.html): the opening paragraph and the sections "Theory" and "Example and interpretation". Stop before "Conditional feature importance".
- IML, [Leave One Feature Out (LOFO) Importance](https://christophm.github.io/interpretable-ml-book/lofo.html): from the start of the chapter through "Examples", then the section "LOFO versus PFI". The lecture calls this method leave-one-covariate-out (LOCO); it is the same thing.

Optional, deeper: ESL section 10.13, pp. 367–370 (relative importance of predictors and partial dependence plots); ESL section 9.1.1, pp. 297–299 (the backfitting algorithm); Hooker, G., Mentch, L. and Zhou, S. (2021), "Unrestricted permutation forces extrapolation: variable importance requires at least one more model, or there is no free variable importance", *Statistics and Computing* 31(6), article 82, [doi:10.1007/s11222-021-10057-z](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11222-021-10057-z); Lei, J., G'Sell, M., Rinaldo, A., Tibshirani, R. J. and Wasserman, L. (2018), "Distribution-free predictive inference for regression", *Journal of the American Statistical Association* 113(523), 1094–1111, section 6 only, [doi:10.1080/01621459.2017.1307116](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2017.1307116).
